summary: All registered obligations remain disposed (three confirmed in-scope violations plus one reviewed bounded no-violation) with no pending work and no open review issues, and new obligation capacity is exhausted; this step therefore uses the remaining source budget to correct a misleading boundary in my own map. Submission is action=research carrying draft/map.json (base version now 3, so the accepted result becomes v4) with new transport sources, two map changes and sourced feedback. The correction: the v1 Transport surface labelled net_transport.go, tcp_transport.go and inmem_transport.go as externalized on the ground that the library 'does not implement the wire', but those files are in-repository Transport implementations (NetworkTransport and its NewNetworkTransport variants, TCPTransport and its NewTCPTransport variants, InmemTransport) that this run never read, and target_profile.selection_injection repeated the same false claim ('the library neither opens sockets nor chooses durability'). The surface is now deferred with empty behavior_ids and sources pointing at the declarations that show the library ships them, and a separate externalized surface records the Transport interface contract the protocol handlers actually assume (message delivery to the Consumer channel plus the RPC set), keeping the library's reliance on that contract distinct from the unread implementations. target_profile now states that FSM/LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore are always caller-injected while Transport is injected too but also shipped by the library, and its unknowns record that the in-repo transports were not read. Feedback cites the three transport declarations plus the replication and client-API ranges, states this is a boundary correction rather than new protocol knowledge, notes that the other externalized surfaces (caller FSM determinism and durable stores) were not re-checked file by file, and keeps the previously recorded open items (installSnapshot reachability, the compacted-leader variant, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences). Two preflight iterations were needed and are recorded honestly: the map base version had to match accepted v3, and the classification change is impact meaning rather than clarification. Preflight validation now returns valid with no diagnostics.
